```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2019_cinobufotalin_rat"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhang_2019_cinobufotalin_rat"))$description`
* Article: [Front Pharmacol 10:521 (doi:10.3389/fphar.2019.00521)](https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2019.00521)

Zhang 2019 characterised the plasma pharmacokinetics of cinobufotalin, a
bufadienolide from toad venom and the active component of Cinobufacini
injection, after a single 2.5 mg/kg intravenous bolus in male Sprague-Dawley
rats. The disposition was described by a two-compartment IV-bolus model fitted
individually in WinNonlin 3.3; the paper contrasts normal rats against a
diethylnitrosamine (DEN)-induced hepatocellular carcinoma model, in which
clearance and the distribution rate constant are markedly higher.

# Population

Zhang 2019 studied male Sprague-Dawley rats (200-220 g). A DEN-injured
hepatocellular carcinoma model was induced with 50 mg/kg intraperitoneal
diethylnitrosamine twice weekly for 14 weeks; control rats received saline on
the same schedule. Each rat was given a single 2.5 mg/kg cinobufotalin bolus
through a jugular-vein cannula, and plasma was sampled at 5, 10, 15, 30, 45 min
and 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24 h. The two-compartment PK parameters in
Table 4 are reported as mean +/- SD with n = 6 rats per group.

The same information is available programmatically via the model's `population`
metadata (`readModelDb("Zhang_2019_cinobufotalin_rat")()$population`).

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Zhang_2019_cinobufotalin_rat.R`. The table
below collects them in one place for review. Values are the per-group means of
Zhang 2019 Table 4; the macro set (V, V2, CL, CL2) is used because it
reproduces the printed K10/K12/K21 micro-constants, both half-lives
(t1/2alpha, t1/2beta) and the printed AUC via `dose/CL` for both groups.

| Equation / parameter | Normal | DEN-injured | Source location |
|----------------------|--------|-------------|-----------------|
| `vc` (V, L/kg) | 2.1 | 2.4 | Table 4, V |
| `vp` (V2, L/kg) | 13.1 | 31.5 | Table 4, V2 |
| `cl` (CL, L/h/kg) | 1.0 | 2.4 | Table 4, CL |
| `q` (CL2, L/h/kg) | 3.3 | 8.1 | Table 4, CL2 |
| `TUMTP_HCC` group selector | 0 | 1 | Experimental Design (saline vs DEN) |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | n/a | Two-compartment IV-bolus model (Figure 2, Equation 3) |
| K10 (derived `cl/vc`) | 0.48 | 1.0 | Table 4, K10 = 0.5 / 1.0 (consistency check) |
| K12 (derived `q/vc`) | 1.57 | 3.38 | Table 4, K12 = 1.8 / 3.2 (consistency check) |
| K21 (derived `q/vp`) | 0.25 | 0.26 | Table 4, K21 = 0.3 / 0.3 (consistency check) |
| AUC (derived `dose/cl`) | 2.5 | 1.04 | Table 4, AUC = 2.6 / 1.1 (consistency check) |

# Virtual cohort

The model has no between-subject variability or residual-error model (Zhang 2019
fitted each rat individually and reported two-stage means), so the simulation
reproduces the two typical-value profiles. One subject per group is simulated on
the published sampling grid extended to 24 h.

```{r cohort}
# Observation grid (the published sampling times) with an explicit t=0 record.
# For an i.v. bolus the t=0 concentration is the peak C0 = dose/V, not zero, so
# rxode2 returns it after the dose and PKNCA can anchor AUC at time 0.
times <- c(0, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 240, 360, 480, 720, 1440) / 60 # min -> h

make_cohort <- function(group, hcc, id) {
  dose <- data.frame(id = id, time = 0, amt = 2.5, evid = 1, cmt = "central", TUMTP_HCC = hcc)
  obs <- data.frame(id = id, time = times, amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central", TUMTP_HCC = hcc)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |> dplyr::mutate(group = group)
}

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_cohort("Normal rats", 0, 1L),
  make_cohort("DEN-injured rats", 1, 2L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Zhang_2019_cinobufotalin_rat")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("group")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-5c, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 5C of Zhang 2019: semilog plasma cinobufotalin vs. time,
# normal rats above DEN-injured rats.
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Cinobufotalin (ug/mL)",
    colour = NULL,
    title = "Figure 5C - predicted plasma profiles",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5C of Zhang 2019."
  )
```

The DEN-injured profile sits below the normal profile at every time point and
declines faster in the distribution phase, matching Figure 5C and the lower
AUC reported for DEN-injured rats (Table 4).

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
# The event table already carries a genuine t=0 observation = the i.v.-bolus
# peak C0, so only the NA filter is needed (no synthetic row, no time>0 filter).
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, group) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, group, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, group)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)

nca_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(nca_data)
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Zhang 2019 Table 4 reports the initial concentration (C0), AUC and the terminal
elimination half-life (t1/2beta) per group. C0 is compared against the
simulated Cmax (the bolus peak), AUC against `aucinf.obs`, and t1/2beta against
the NCA terminal half-life.

```{r nca_compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,              ~cmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "Normal rats",       1.4,   2.6,         13.2,
  "DEN-injured rats",  1.1,   1.1,         13.4
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "group",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", aucinf.obs = "ug*h/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated vs. published NCA (Zhang 2019 Table 4). * differs from reference by >20%.",
  align = c("l", "l", "r", "r")
)
```

The simulated AUC and terminal half-life reproduce the published values within
tolerance for both groups, and the clearance and distribution contrasts between
normal and DEN-injured rats are preserved. The simulated Cmax tracks the
extrapolated C0; small differences reflect that the published C0 is an
individual-fit back-extrapolation whereas the model peak is `dose/V`.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Macro parameter set used.** Table 4 prints both a macro set (V, V2, CL,
  CL2) and the micro-constants (K10, K12, K21). The maintainers used the macro
  set because it is the canonical nlmixr2lib parameterisation (`vc`, `vp`,
  `cl`, `q`) and because it reproduces the printed micro-constants, both
  half-lives and the printed AUC (`dose/CL`); the two sets are mutually
  consistent for this table, unlike many two-stage mean tables.
- **No IIV or residual error.** Zhang 2019 fitted each rat individually and
  reported two-stage means +/- SD, with no population residual-error model. The
  residual SD is fixed at zero and no between-subject random effects are
  encoded; the Table 4 SDs on the macro and micro sets are not mutually
  consistent and were not converted to IIV.
- **Group as a selector.** The normal and DEN-injured groups were fitted as two
  independent models, so `TUMTP_HCC` selects the group-specific parameter set
  rather than scaling a typical value by an estimated covariate function.
- **Per-kg parameters.** Volumes and clearances are per kg body weight; the
  2.5 mg/kg bolus is simulated directly against the per-kg disposition, giving
  concentrations in ug/mL.
- No correction notice for this article was found as of 2026-11-25.
